_meta.keyKnowledge: We are learning about how the nature of work is changing in Australia and what predictions experts make about the future of work.

toLevel2.question: Technology, automation, and artificial intelligence are reshaping many Australian jobs across recent decades.
toLevel2.correct: True
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Technology, automation, and AI are reshaping many Australian jobs in recent decades.

distractors.answer: False
distractors.explanation: This pattern is widely documented in current Australian labour-market reports.

toLevel2.question: The nature of work in Australia has no link to any change driven by technology in any sector.
toLevel2.correct: False
toLevel2.correctExplanation: The nature of work has changed substantially due to technology over recent decades in Australia.

distractors.answer: True
distractors.explanation: Treating work as unchanged by technology ignores documented shifts in Australian workplaces.

toLevel2.question: Some Australian industries are growing while others are declining, shifting where new jobs become available.
toLevel2.correct: True
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Some industries grow while others decline, shifting where new jobs become available across Australia.

distractors.answer: False
distractors.explanation: Industry growth and decline patterns are widely documented at this level.

toLevel2.question: The gig economy and flexible work arrangements have no presence in Australia at all.
toLevel2.correct: False
toLevel2.correctExplanation: The gig economy and flexible work arrangements have grown across many Australian sectors.

distractors.answer: True
distractors.explanation: Treating the gig economy as absent ignores its documented presence in Australia.

toLevel2.question: Future-of-work reports often highlight adaptability, digital literacy, and problem-solving as valuable skills.
toLevel2.correct: True
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Adaptability, digital literacy, and problem-solving are widely highlighted as valuable future-of-work skills.

distractors.answer: False
distractors.explanation: These three skills appear regularly in future-of-work reports.

toLevel2.question: Remote work in Australia has remained exactly the same as before any global pandemic.
toLevel2.correct: False
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Remote work patterns have shifted substantially in Australia since the pandemic of 2020.

distractors.answer: True
distractors.explanation: Treating remote work as unchanged ignores documented shifts in Australian workplaces since 2020.

toLevel2.question: Automation can replace some routine tasks while creating new roles in design, maintenance, and oversight.
toLevel2.correct: True
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Automation replaces some routine tasks but also creates new roles in design, maintenance, and oversight.

distractors.answer: False
distractors.explanation: This pattern is widely documented in future-of-work analysis.

toLevel2.question: Predictions about future jobs always say every job will disappear and no new jobs will appear.
toLevel2.correct: False
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Most future-of-work predictions say some jobs will disappear and others will appear.

distractors.answer: True
distractors.explanation: Treating predictions as universal job loss misstates the standard analysis.

toLevel2.question: Digital literacy is widely listed as one of the most important skills in Australian future-of-work reports.
toLevel2.correct: True
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Digital literacy is widely listed as a core skill in Australian future-of-work reports.

distractors.answer: False
distractors.explanation: Digital literacy is consistently emphasised in current future-of-work analysis.

toLevel2.question: The rise of the gig economy has no link to any change in how Australians find paid work.
toLevel2.correct: False
toLevel2.correctExplanation: The gig economy has changed how many Australians find paid work, especially through digital platforms.

distractors.answer: True
distractors.explanation: Treating the gig economy as having no link ignores documented changes in how work is found.

toLevel2.question: Adaptability has no link to how workers respond to changes in technology, industry, or the broader economy.
toLevel2.correct: False
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Adaptability supports workers responding to changes in technology, industry, and the broader economy.

distractors.answer: True
distractors.explanation: Treating adaptability as unlinked to change ignores its core role in future-of-work skill lists.

toLevel2.question: Knowing how work is changing has no link to any career or study choice a young person makes.
toLevel2.correct: False
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Knowing how work is changing supports more informed choices about study, training, and careers.

distractors.answer: True
distractors.explanation: Treating this knowledge as unrelated to choices ignores its core role in career planning.

toLevel2.question: Which of the following best describes how technology is changing Australian work today?
toLevel2.correct: Technology, automation, and AI are reshaping many jobs by changing the tasks workers do day to day
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Technology, automation, and AI are reshaping many jobs by changing day-to-day tasks.

distractors.answer: Technology has no link to any Australian job in any sector and never has any effect at all
distractors.explanation: Technology is closely linked to Australian work; the link is direct.

distractors.answer: Technology has frozen every Australian job exactly as it was in 1990 and prevented any change
distractors.explanation: Technology has driven substantial change since 1990; jobs are not frozen at that point.

distractors.answer: Technology has eliminated every Australian job in every sector and replaced all work with full automation
distractors.explanation: Technology has not eliminated all jobs; many roles continue alongside automation.

toLevel2.question: Which of the following best describes the gig economy?
toLevel2.correct: Short, task-based work organised through digital platforms with flexible hours and per-task pay
toLevel2.correctExplanation: The gig economy is short, task-based work organised through digital platforms with flexible hours.

distractors.answer: A long-term salaried role at a single employer with the same fixed annual pay across many years
distractors.explanation: Long-term salaried roles describe traditional employment, not gig work.

distractors.answer: A volunteering role at a community organisation for unpaid hours each week throughout the year
distractors.explanation: Volunteering is unpaid; gig work is paid per task.

distractors.answer: A child's chore payment received for tidying a bedroom each Saturday morning across a childhood
distractors.explanation: Pocket money for chores is not standard gig economy work.

toLevel2.question: Which industries are widely listed as growing in Australia at present?
toLevel2.correct: Health care, technology, and renewable energy are listed as growing and adding jobs across regions
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Health care, technology, and renewable energy are widely listed as growing Australian industries.

distractors.answer: Every industry in every Australian region is shrinking at exactly the same rate this year
distractors.explanation: Australian industries grow at different rates; treating all as shrinking equally is wrong.

distractors.answer: Only one industry in Australia is growing at present and every other sector has stopped operating
distractors.explanation: Multiple industries are growing in Australia; the single-industry claim is wrong.

distractors.answer: No Australian industry is growing or shrinking and every sector has stayed the same since 1990
distractors.explanation: Industries do change over time; treating them as frozen since 1990 is wrong.

toLevel2.question: Which skills are widely highlighted in Australian future-of-work reports?
toLevel2.correct: Adaptability, digital literacy, and problem-solving are highlighted as increasingly valuable across many sectors
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Adaptability, digital literacy, and problem-solving are widely highlighted in future-of-work reports.

distractors.answer: Reports never mention any skill at all in any year and have no link to any future Australian role
distractors.explanation: Predictions discuss skills directly; treating them as never mentioning skills is wrong.

distractors.answer: Reports always say every job will require only one identical skill across every Australian workplace
distractors.explanation: Predictions describe many different valuable skills, not a single identical one.

distractors.answer: Reports always say no skill will matter in any Australian role at any stage of any career path
distractors.explanation: Predictions list many skills as mattering; the no-skill claim is wrong.

toLevel2.question: How has remote work changed in Australia since the pandemic?
toLevel2.correct: Many Australian workers now spend more time working from home than they did before 2020
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Many Australian workers now spend more time working from home than they did before 2020.

distractors.answer: Remote work is exactly the same as it was before 2020 in every Australian workplace today
distractors.explanation: Remote work patterns have shifted; the no-change claim is wrong.

distractors.answer: Remote work has been banned in every Australian workplace since 2020 and no Australian works from home
distractors.explanation: Remote work has not been banned; many Australians work from home today.

distractors.answer: Remote work has replaced every office-based job in Australia and no worker attends any workplace
distractors.explanation: Many Australians still attend workplaces; remote work has not replaced all office-based jobs.

toLevel2.question: How does automation affect jobs in many Australian workplaces?
toLevel2.correct: Automation can replace some routine tasks while creating new roles in design, maintenance, and oversight
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Automation replaces some routine tasks while creating new roles in design, maintenance, and oversight.

distractors.answer: Automation has no link to any job in any Australian workplace and never has any effect at any time
distractors.explanation: Automation is closely linked to many Australian jobs; the link is direct.

distractors.answer: Automation always replaces every Australian worker and never leaves any role for any human being
distractors.explanation: Automation does not replace every worker; many roles continue alongside automated systems.

distractors.answer: Automation always creates the same jobs that it replaces in every Australian workplace each year
distractors.explanation: Automation creates different new roles, not the exact same jobs it replaces.

toLevel2.question: Why is digital literacy widely seen as an increasingly valuable skill?
toLevel2.correct: Many growing roles use digital tools, data, and online systems, so digital literacy improves placement
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Many growing roles use digital tools and data; digital literacy improves placement for these jobs.

distractors.answer: Digital literacy has no link to any Australian job in any sector and never affects placement at all
distractors.explanation: Digital literacy is closely linked to many Australian jobs.

distractors.answer: Digital literacy is identical in every job and so it never affects which workers are better placed
distractors.explanation: Digital literacy varies across roles; treating it as identical everywhere is wrong.

distractors.answer: Digital literacy always reduces a worker's chance of finding any Australian job at any time at all
distractors.explanation: Digital literacy usually improves rather than reduces job prospects.

toLevel2.question: Which of the following is the best example of an industry currently in decline in some Australian regions?
toLevel2.correct: Traditional print newspapers, where digital news has reduced demand for printed copies in many local markets
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Traditional print newspapers have declined in many regions because digital news has reduced demand.

distractors.answer: Renewable energy generation, which has expanded across Australia with new solar and wind projects recently
distractors.explanation: Renewable energy generation is growing rather than declining in Australia.

distractors.answer: Health care services, which have grown to support an ageing population in many Australian regions today
distractors.explanation: Health care has grown rather than declined in recent years.

distractors.answer: Software development, which has expanded in most Australian capital cities and major regional centres recently
distractors.explanation: Software development has expanded rather than declined in recent years.

toLevel2.question: Why might a young person benefit from understanding the changing nature of work?
toLevel2.correct: Knowing how work is changing supports informed choices about study, training, and future career paths
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Knowing how work is changing supports informed choices about study, training, and future career paths.

distractors.answer: Knowing how work is changing has no link to any choice a young person makes at any career stage
distractors.explanation: This knowledge is closely linked to many career and study choices.

distractors.answer: Knowing how work is changing always guarantees a fixed lifetime salary in every Australian workplace
distractors.explanation: Knowledge supports planning; it does not guarantee a fixed lifetime salary.

distractors.answer: Knowing how work is changing always removes every choice from every young person planning a career
distractors.explanation: This knowledge expands rather than removes choice.

toLevel2.question: Which scenario best illustrates the gig economy in Australia?

toLevel2.correctExplanation: App-based delivery work paid per delivery on flexible hours is a clear example of gig economy work.

distractors.explanation: Volunteering is unpaid; gig work is paid per task.

distractors.answer: A child receives pocket money from a parent for tidying a bedroom each Saturday morning
distractors.explanation: Pocket money for chores is not standard gig economy work.

toLevel2.question: Why does adaptability matter as a skill for the future of Australian work?
toLevel2.correct: Industries, technologies, and roles change across a working life, so adaptable workers adjust more easily
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Industries, technologies, and roles change across a working life; adaptable workers adjust more easily.

distractors.answer: Adaptability has no link to any Australian job in any sector and never affects how workers respond
distractors.explanation: Adaptability is closely linked to many Australian jobs.

distractors.answer: Adaptability always reduces a worker's chance of finding any job in every Australian sector each year
distractors.explanation: Adaptability usually improves rather than reduces job prospects.

distractors.answer: Adaptability always guarantees a fixed lifetime salary in every Australian workplace at every stage
distractors.explanation: Adaptability supports adjustment; it does not guarantee a fixed lifetime salary.

toLevel2.question: Which list includes only documented future-of-work skills in Australian reports?
toLevel2.correct: Adaptability, digital literacy, problem-solving, communication, and the ability to work in teams effectively
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Adaptability, digital literacy, problem-solving, communication, and teamwork are widely documented future-of-work skills.

distractors.answer: Office wall colours, free public concerts, and other items unrelated to skills in any Australian report
distractors.explanation: Office colours and free concerts have no link to documented future-of-work skills.

distractors.answer: Random outcomes and fixed quantities by chance with no link between any skill and any Australian worker
distractors.explanation: Skills are linked to workers and sectors; treating skill development as random is wrong.

distractors.answer: Punishment, fear, and refusal of any skill development at any time in any Australian workplace at all
distractors.explanation: Punishment and fear are not documented future-of-work skills.
